keyVerseText: So David would not remove the ark of the LORD unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite.
rootMeaning: The name עֹבֵד אֱדוֹם (ʻÔbêd ʼĔdôwm) derives from the Hebrew root עָבַד (ʻâbad), meaning to serve, work, or labor, combined with אֱדֹם (Edom), which may refer to the nation of Edom or mean "man." Literally, the name can be understood as "servant of Edom" or "worker of Edom." This etymology highlights a personal identity tied to service, possibly indicating a role of devoted labor or servanthood, which surpasses a mere label and points to a life of purposeful dedication.
usageInScripture: The term עֹבֵד אֱדוֹם appears twenty times in Scripture, predominantly translated as "of Obededom" or simply "Obededom," reflecting its use as a proper name. It refers to five Israelites, including a notable Levite and Gittite who safeguarded the ark of the LORD after Uzzah's death, as well as a Merarite Levite involved in temple music and gatekeeping. The consistency of the name's translation underscores its significance as a personal name linked with faithful service to God, especially in roles connected to the sanctuary and worship.
theologicalSignificance: The name Obededom, meaning "servant of Edom," carries profound theological weight as it embodies the biblical theme of faithful service to God. The individuals bearing this name were entrusted with sacred duties, such as guarding the ark and ministering in the temple, illustrating that God calls and equips servants from diverse backgrounds for His purposes. This reminds believers that true worship involves devoted service and stewardship of God's presence. Moreover, the preservation of the ark in Obededom's house signifies God's blessing upon those who serve Him faithfully, reinforcing the Christian conviction that obedience and reverence toward God invite His favor and protection.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 6:10, the ark of the LORD is placed in the house of Obededom the Gittite after Uzzah's death, emphasizing Obededom's role as a faithful caretaker. The use of the name here highlights the significance of a servant who provides refuge for the holy presence of God. This moment underscores the importance of reverent service and the blessing that accompanies it, as Obededom's household becomes a sanctuary for the ark, illustrating the tangible reality of God's protection over those who honor Him through obedient service.
